script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The list is broad, but saying Moses leaves no corner of daily life out goes beyond what the passage states.
The notepad joke makes light of a warning that includes suffering for children.
The verse speaks of all they put their hand to, not literally everything their hands touch.
Losing a hat is not a fitting comparison for people fleeing defeat, and the joke makes light of a serious warning.
The verse says Israel will be an object of horror; it does not say nobody will be afraid of them.
The imagined bakery joke does not match the situation: imagining a building is not the same as building one and being unable to live in it.
The verse does not say the house still stands; it leaves what happens to the house open.
Moses says the planter will not enjoy the fruit, not that someone else gets the harvest.
Saying he will not joke comments on how he tells the passage.
The verse calls them gods of wood and stone but does not say people carved them.
The frog joke makes light of a warning about a lost harvest and does not fit the action being described.
The verse says the foreigner will rise higher, but does not say he will stay in the land for good.
Saying the servant answer is the other way around implies Israel will become the foreigner's servant. The passage describes lending and their relative positions, not that servitude.
Enemies and neighbors are not close in sound, so the comparison does not make sense.
The passage does not say that not understanding the language makes the situation more frightening.
No respect for the old and no pity for the young does not necessarily mean neither group is spared.
Deuteronomy 28:51 is the preceding verse, not the next verse.
Saying he will let the passage stand comments on how he tells it.
Saying he will not joke comments on how he tells the passage.
The verse says no one will buy them; it does not say nobody frees them.
